dispositions.rationale: Dispatch is the invoking agent's act and no suite can observe it. The spec says so in ARO-D2 and lists it under Out of scope. ARO-A12 and ARO-A13 pin the two ends a suite can observe, and the record attests to the dispatch between them. The parent's ACQ-A22 is served to that extent, and the limit is reported to the owner.

make content-tests discovers every suite under src, and this slice does not touch that discovery. A criterion on which suites the gate runs would pin the gate's own implementation, which is outside a slice that changes four lists and adds tests.

Already covered. The registry is the set of lens directories holding a prompt.md, so a lens whose prompt.md is absent is out of the registry, and ARO-A2 fails on any set other than the four. The what-if section now says so.

Outside this slice. The record check deliberately keeps a round closed when a lens it ran is later retired from the registry, so refusing a report from a lens outside the registry would reverse existing behaviour the slice does not change. Out of scope now says so.

Already covered. ARO-A11 requires each lens's prompt to carry exactly its row of the ARO-D1 table, and no row is empty, so a lens with an empty enforces list fails it. The what-if section now says so.

parts.statement: Every rule in the standard appears exactly once across the source `enforces` lists, including after rules are added.
The source lists assign each rule to the lens specified by ARO-D1.

obligations.source: “Every rule of the acceptance-criteria standard gets exactly one owning lens” and “ARO-D1 — Every rule has exactly one owning lens,” followed by the ownership table.
obligations.statement: Every rule has exactly one owner, with ownership assigned according to ARO-D1.

parts.statement: An emitted prompt is the lens body plus the four shared contracts, byte for byte.
An emitted prompt contains exactly the rules named by that lens's `enforces` list.
Each emitted prompt contains the exact rule allocation stated in ARO-D1.

obligations.source: “The emitter puts exactly those rules into the lens's prompt” and “The emitter suite and the checker suite pin three things: how a prompt is composed…”
obligations.statement: Each emitted lens prompt preserves its composition and contains the rules owned by that lens.

parts.statement: An objection citing a rule outside its reporting lens's ownership is refused.
Each of the six newly assigned rules passes ownership validation when cited by its owning lens.
Each of the eleven previously assigned rules continues to pass ownership validation when cited by its owning lens.

obligations.source: “The record check accepts an objection from the lens only under those rules” and “every rule has a lens that can object under it.”
obligations.statement: The record checker enforces ownership while allowing every rule's owner to object under that rule.

parts.statement: The lens registry contains exactly behavioural-outcome, obligation-reduction, set-consistency and what-if.
The emitted round names those four lenses and contains exactly one prompt for each.
A record cannot close as complete without a report from every one of the four lenses.

obligations.source: “The suites can observe the two ends of it: the round the emitter writes, and the record the check closes. ARO-A12 and ARO-A13 pin those.”
obligations.statement: The observable dispatch surface consists of exactly four lenses at both emission and record closure.

parts.statement: A lens naming a rule absent from the standard is refused as `no-lenses` with nothing written.
An empty lens registry is refused as `no-lenses` with nothing written.
An absent standard is refused as `no-standard` with nothing written.

obligations.source: The current state says the emitter “refuses a lens that names a rule the standard lacks,” and ARO-D2 identifies the existing emitter failures as preservation criteria.
obligations.statement: Invalid or missing emitter configuration is refused without producing output.

parts.statement: An objection with a missing or blank target, ground rule or scenario part is refused as `schema`.
An objection containing a field outside the objection schema is refused as `schema`.

obligations.source: “This spec serves seven parent criteria: ACQ-A20 … in full” and “The emitter suite and the checker suite pin … what the record check refuses.”
obligations.statement: The record checker preserves the objection-schema refusal surface assigned to this spec by ACQ-A20.

parts.statement: Missing or schema-invalid obligation-reduction workings are refused as `invalid-workings`.
An undischarged obligation part without a corresponding objection is refused as `unreported-residue`.
A ground outside the reporting lens's ownership is refused as `ground-outside-lens`.

obligations.source: “The checker suite … already pins the `invalid-workings`, `unreported-residue` and `ground-outside-lens` refusals.”
obligations.statement: The checker preserves its existing obligation-reduction record-integrity refusals.

parts.statement: Two emissions from the same unchanged tree and document are byte-identical.

obligations.source: “Deterministic suites check them” and ARO-D2 identifies ARO-A17 as an existing preservation criterion.
obligations.statement: Prompt emission from unchanged inputs remains deterministic.

parts.statement: The existing tests for ARO-A3, ARO-A4, ARO-A5, ARO-A8, ARO-A9, ARO-A10, ARO-A15, ARO-A16 and ARO-A17 remain passing.

obligations.source: “Nine of the criteria below name tests that exist today … They already pass. They are preservation criteria, and they must still pass after the `enforces` lists change.”
obligations.statement: The nine existing emitter and checker tests continue to pass after the ownership-list change.

parts.statement: Tests are added for ARO-A1, ARO-A2, ARO-A6, ARO-A7 and ARO-A11 through ARO-A14.
A test is added for ARO-A18, which is also outside the stated set of nine criteria with existing tests.

obligations.source: “The slice adds a test for each other criterion where none exists.”
obligations.statement: The slice adds a test for every criterion that does not already have one.

ground.reason: The scope says the criteria attack runs four reviewers, and ARO-D2 promises to pin which lenses run. ARO-A12 checks only the emitted round and prompt files, while ARO-A13 checks only that reports are present. The document explicitly says no suite observes dispatch. These artifacts can exist without any reviewer executing.

objections.objection: No criterion verifies that the four lenses actually run; emitted prompts and present reports stand in for execution.
objections.obligation: The criteria attack runs behavioural-outcome, obligation-reduction, set-consistency and what-if.

scenario.expect: ARO-A12 and ARO-A13 pass while one or more of the four reviewers never run.
scenario.given: The emitter writes four correctly named prompts and a record contains four well-formed synthetic reports.
scenario.when: The emitter and record-checker suites inspect the round and record.

ground.reason: ARO-D1 promises that the record check accepts objections under rules owned by their lens. ARO-A14 checks only that one particular refusal, ground-outside-lens, is absent. It does not require acceptance or exclude another refusal.

objections.objection: ARO-A14 lets the checker reject a newly supported objection for another reason while satisfying the stated check.
objections.obligation: A well-formed objection citing one of the six newly assigned rules is accepted from its owning lens.

scenario.expect: The ARO-A14 check passes because ground-outside-lens is absent, while the objection remains rejected and cannot be reported.
scenario.given: A well-formed objection from the assigned lens cites one of the six newly assigned rules, but the checker returns a different refusal.
scenario.when: The checker suite tests only for the absence of ground-outside-lens.

ground.reason: ARO-A18 promises that no other content suite regresses but checks only that make content-tests exits 0. A green aggregate gate does not establish that every relevant suite still runs or that its preserved behaviour remains covered.

objections.objection: ARO-A18 lets an omitted or bypassed content suite lose its guarantee while the aggregate command remains green.
objections.obligation: Changing the ownership lists causes no regression in any other content suite.

scenario.expect: make content-tests exits 0 while an omitted content suite or the behaviour it preserves has regressed.
scenario.given: The deliverable causes an existing content suite to be skipped by the aggregate gate.
scenario.when: ARO-A18 runs only make content-tests and judges success from its exit status.

ground.reason: The criteria check ownership eligibility only for the six newly assigned rules. They do not preserve the owning lenses' ability to object under the eleven existing assignments.

objections.objection: The record checker may reject a well-formed objection under any previously assigned rule while every criterion still passes.

scenario.expect: The objection passes ownership validation because its ground belongs to the reporting lens.
scenario.given: The ownership lists and emitted prompts match ARO-D1, but the checker rejects a well-formed objection from an owning lens when it cites one of the eleven previously assigned rules.
scenario.when: All acceptance checks run, including ARO-A14 for the six new assignments and ARO-A18.

ground.reason: ARO-D2 promises a new test for every criterion that lacks one, which includes ARO-A18, but no criterion requires such a test to be added.

objections.objection: The slice can pass while adding no test for ARO-A18, contrary to the stated test-addition commitment.

scenario.expect: The added test inventory contains a test for ARO-A18, or the design excludes ARO-A18 from the test-addition promise.
scenario.given: Tests are added for ARO-A1, ARO-A2, ARO-A6, ARO-A7 and ARO-A11 through ARO-A14, but no test is added for ARO-A18.
scenario.when: The acceptance checks run and `make content-tests` exits 0.

ground.reason: "has no report in it" does not say whether a lens whose report is the empty report (report: "empty", no objections) counts as having a report. One reading treats the empty report as a report and closes the record; the other treats it as no report and blocks every clean attack from ever closing.

objections.objection: ARO-A13 leaves open whether a record in which a lens filed an empty report is complete or incomplete, so two implementations of the record check diverge on the terminal state of a clean attack: one closes it, the other reports the record incomplete and names the lens that found nothing.

scenario.expect: under the "empty report is a report" reading the record is complete and the check closes it; under the "empty report is no report" reading the check reports the record incomplete, naming the what-if lens, and no clean attack can ever close
scenario.given: An attack round over a document whose criteria draw no objection from the what-if lens, so its report in the record is {"report": "empty", "objections": []}, while the other three lenses each filed objection-bearing reports
scenario.when: the record check judges the record against ARO-A13

ground.reason: ARO-A16 refuses an absent standard, and ARO-A2 pins the registry's lens set, but nothing covers the lens's own prompt body being absent: the emitter reads each lens's prompt.md to compose prompts (ARO-A3), and no criterion states what happens when that file is missing while the registry still names the lens.

objections.objection: The criteria let through an emitter that crashes, hangs, or silently writes a partial round when a registered lens's prompt.md is absent, because no criterion pins a refusal for a missing lens body the way ARO-A16 pins one for a missing standard.

scenario.expect: A named refusal with nothing written, mirroring the no-standard behaviour of ARO-A16, or an explicit decision that this case is out of scope.
scenario.given: The lens registry names the four lenses, the standard is present, but one lens's prompt.md file is missing from lenses/.

ground.reason: ARO-A13 refuses a record missing one of the four lenses' reports, but the symmetric case of a record carrying a report from a lens outside the registry is neither covered nor ruled out: the check could accept, ignore, or mangle the extra report and every criterion still passes.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a record check that accepts a record polluted by a report from an unknown fifth lens, so a stale or forged report could survive into the closed record unexamined.

scenario.expect: The record check refuses the record, naming the unknown lens, by the same completeness discipline ARO-A13 states.
scenario.given: A record containing well-formed reports for all four registered lenses plus a report from a lens the registry does not hold.

ground.reason: ARO-A1 requires each rule the standard holds to appear exactly once, and ARO-A4 pins that a prompt carries exactly its lens's rules, but a lens whose enforces list is empty satisfies both vacuously: the standard's rules can all be owned while one lens owns none, and no criterion states whether that is refused or allowed.

objections.objection: The criteria let through an attack that emits a prompt carrying zero rules for a lens, so the round runs a reviewer that can object under nothing while every criterion passes.

scenario.expect: A recorded decision: either the emitter refuses an empty enforces list, naming the lens, or the spec states that a rule-less lens is allowed and what such a prompt may report.
scenario.given: A source tree where every rule of the standard appears exactly once across the lists, but one lens's enforces list is empty.
scenario.when: The emitter suite runs its ownership checks.
